subject.title: [Bug]: One-shot run cleanup leaks codex app-server process (inverted closeAndWait condition) → duplicate app-servers → spurious turn_aborted

question: Should maintainers require current-main macOS process-count proof before changing one-shot Codex app-server cleanup semantics, or accept the reporter's 2026.7.1-beta.2 evidence to queue a narrow fix now?
rationale: Current source confirms the challenged guard, but current close() already schedules a force-kill fallback and the active-lease behavior overlaps another open Codex lifecycle report, so automation should not choose the proof bar or cleanup semantics alone.

options.title: Require current-main macOS proof
options.body: Run or request a current-main one-shot process-count repro before choosing the cleanup change, while keeping this issue open as the focused report.

options.title: Queue narrow cleanup repair now
options.body: Treat the beta evidence as sufficient and repair the retire/closeAndWait invariant with tests for idle, unmatched, and active-lease cases.

options.title: Fold into broader lifecycle work
options.body: Track the close condition under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99947 only if maintainers want one broader Codex shared-client lifecycle fix instead of a focused process-leak issue.

recommendation.title: Require current-main macOS proof
recommendation.body: Run or request a current-main one-shot process-count repro before choosing the cleanup change, while keeping this issue open as the focused report.

likelyOwner.reason: They approved the merged one-shot teardown default and have recent Codex run-attempt commits in this lifecycle area.
